method: Manual point-in-time extraction from registered official issuer disclosures. Summaries are paraphrases; locators permit reconstruction.

extractions.locator: Reserves composition; How we manage USDC
extractions.evidence_summary: Circle reports that USDC reserves consist of bank deposits, short-dated US Treasuries, and overnight Treasury repos; most reserves are held through the Circle Reserve Fund and the balance is primarily cash at large banks.
extractions.limitations: Composition is issuer-reported and changes after the stated date. Exact weights must come from the dated reserve report used in estimation.

extractions.locator: Monthly assurance and transparency; Independently audited
extractions.evidence_summary: Circle identifies weekly reserve disclosures and monthly third-party assurance under AICPA attestation standards, and identifies Deloitte as its independent auditor.
extractions.limitations: An assurance engagement is narrower than a continuous audit and applies to the report date and criteria stated in the linked report.

extractions.locator: USDC; Redeeming USDC; User Type A and User Type B
extractions.evidence_summary: Direct 1:1 redemption is contractual for eligible Circle Mint users with accounts in good standing, subject to possession, compliance, applicable law, and fees; other users must redeem through an eligible intermediary or obtain an eligible account.
extractions.limitations: Direct issuer redemption is not universally available to retail holders.

extractions.locator: Stability you can trust; reserve-composition footnotes
extractions.evidence_summary: Circle states that USDC reserves are held separately from operating funds for the benefit of holders and describes custodial, separately managed, and money-market-fund arrangements used for reserve assets.
extractions.limitations: This is an issuer disclosure of structure, not an independent legal opinion about holder priority in every insolvency scenario.

extractions.locator: Suspension, termination, and service limitations; blockchain-network provisions
extractions.evidence_summary: Circle may delay, reject, suspend, or terminate services for compliance, fraud, legal, security, or operational reasons; supported-network disruptions and forks can also impair transfers or redemptions.
extractions.limitations: The terms enumerate discretion and contingencies but do not provide probabilities or maximum delay durations.

extractions.locator: USDT Reports & Reserves; Q2 2026 Financial Figures and Reserves Report
extractions.evidence_summary: Tether's dated reserve disclosure reports a diversified reserve pool and categorizes the assets supporting issued tokens; the associated Q2 disclosure states that assets exceeded token-related liabilities at the reporting date.
extractions.limitations: The reserve report is a consolidated point-in-time disclosure and includes entities identified in the report; it is not a continuously updated asset ledger.

extractions.locator: USDT Reports & Reserves; Q2 2026 independent assurance report
extractions.evidence_summary: Tether publishes quarterly reserve reports with an independent accounting-firm assurance report; the Q2 2026 disclosure identifies BDO as the practitioner for the June 30 report.
extractions.limitations: Quarter-end assurance is not continuous verification and is limited to the report's entities, criteria, and measurement date.

extractions.locator: Section 2.6, pp. 14-15; Section 6.3, p. 21
extractions.evidence_summary: Issuer redemption is limited to approved KYC-verified customers, currently requires a $100,000 minimum, and carries the greater of a $1,000 or 0.1% fee; primary-market settlement is at face value less fees.
extractions.limitations: Secondary-market holders do not automatically have the same direct issuer relationship, and published fees may change.

extractions.locator: Section 3 Safeguarding Arrangements, p. 16
extractions.evidence_summary: Tether states that sale proceeds are held or invested in a reserve basket, primarily with banks and licensed financial institutions, to meet redemption requests; the document describes Tether's obligation to eligible primary-market customers but does not state a universal holder property claim over segregated assets.
extractions.limitations: The reviewed disclosure does not establish bankruptcy remoteness or a direct reserve claim for all secondary-market holders; this absence must remain visible in scoring.

extractions.locator: Section 2.7, pp. 15-16; Section 6.4, p. 22
extractions.evidence_summary: Tether may reject onboarding and delay or suspend redemption for prohibited use, government direction, investigations, unauthorized-access concerns, fraud, theft, or other criminal activity; it may also freeze, burn, or block tokens under its terms.
extractions.limitations: The disclosure provides broad discretionary and legal triggers without maximum processing times.

extractions.locator: Sections 1.1.1 and 3.1.2
extractions.evidence_summary: Paxos states that PYUSD is backed one-for-one by dollars in custodial accounts, short-dated U.S. government obligations, overnight reverse repos collateralized by those obligations, and qualifying government money-market funds.
extractions.limitations: The terms define permitted asset classes but exact point-in-time weights must come from the applicable monthly report.

extractions.locator: Attestations; 2026 June report; Fostering trust through verification
extractions.evidence_summary: Paxos publishes monthly PYUSD attestations and identifies KPMG as the independent examiner for reports from February 2025 onward under AICPA attestation standards.
extractions.limitations: The separate rapid portfolio reports are management-prepared and unreviewed; the independent attestation applies only to its specified date and criteria.

extractions.locator: Sections 2.2, 2.7, and 2.8
extractions.evidence_summary: Only verified Paxos customers can redeem directly through a Paxos account. Redemption is one-for-one after compliance checks, may be subject to a variable minimum, and has no Paxos redemption fee, although banking, wallet, or transfer charges may apply.
extractions.limitations: Direct issuer access is conditional on account eligibility and jurisdiction; minimums and external fees can change.

extractions.locator: Sections 1.1.1 and 3.1.2
extractions.evidence_summary: Paxos states that assets backing its dollar stablecoins are held in segregated accounts apart from corporate funds on behalf of both customer and non-customer token holders and specifically for their benefit.
extractions.limitations: This records the contractual and custodial structure but is not an independent insolvency-law opinion.

extractions.locator: Sections 1.3, 2.2, 2.3, and 2.6
extractions.evidence_summary: Paxos may restrict services by jurisdiction, suspend minting, refuse issuance or redemption for account, legal, or compliance reasons, cancel defective or suspect orders, and delay withdrawals; blockchain or third-party failures can also disrupt access.
extractions.limitations: Ordinary withdrawals may take up to two days and large withdrawals substantially longer, but no universal maximum is stated.

extractions.locator: Section 2.1(b), RLUSD Reserve
extractions.evidence_summary: The issuer must maintain reserve market value at least equal to outstanding RLUSD using deposits, U.S. Treasury bills with no more than three months remaining, overnight Treasury-collateralized reverse repos, and U.S. government money-market funds.
extractions.limitations: The terms define allowable assets; exact dated weights must be taken from the corresponding monthly attestation.

extractions.locator: Reserve Reports; Attestations; 2026 June report
extractions.evidence_summary: Ripple publishes monthly reports from an independent U.S.-licensed CPA covering management's assertions about RLUSD circulation and reserve composition under AICPA attestation standards.
extractions.limitations: Monthly attestation is point-in-time assurance, not continuous verification of reserve balances.

extractions.evidence_summary: Eligible Ripple customers can redeem RLUSD one-for-one for dollars subject to the separate customer agreement and fees. A holder's redemption right transfers with the token but can be exercised only after the holder qualifies and becomes a customer.
extractions.limitations: The public user terms do not disclose the full customer onboarding requirements, fee schedule, settlement SLA, or operational minimums.

extractions.locator: Section 2.1(b)-(c), RLUSD Reserve and risks
extractions.evidence_summary: Standard Custody states that reserve accounts are segregated from its other assets, while the terms also state that RLUSD does not convey holders a direct or indirect property interest in, or withdrawal right over, specific reserve assets.
extractions.limitations: Segregation and holder property rights are distinct; scoring must not treat the former as proof of the latter or of bankruptcy remoteness.

extractions.locator: Sections 2.2 and 11.1-11.5
extractions.evidence_summary: Ripple may suspend access for regulatory, compliance, fraud, security, or reputational-risk reasons; network failures and forks may halt activity, and addresses or tokens may be frozen, blacklisted, or burned under law or internal compliance policies.
extractions.limitations: The terms provide broad discretion and do not state a maximum suspension or restoration period.

extractions.source_title: First Digital Labs transparency and monthly reserve reports
extractions.locator: Reserve dashboard as of July 31, 2026; Monthly Reserve Reports
extractions.evidence_summary: First Digital reports FDUSD reserves of 75.88% U.S. Treasury bills, 20.42% cash, and 3.70% fixed deposits at July 31, 2026, with reported reserve assets exceeding circulating tokens.
extractions.limitations: Percentages are a point-in-time issuer presentation and must not be backfilled to earlier dates.

extractions.source_title: First Digital Labs transparency and monthly reserve reports
extractions.locator: Monthly Reserve Reports; July 2026 report
extractions.evidence_summary: First Digital publishes monthly independent attestations intended to compare circulating FDUSD with the value of cash and cash-equivalent reserves.
extractions.limitations: Monthly attestation is point-in-time assurance rather than continuous verification; scoring must retain the report's stated scope.

extractions.locator: Sections 3.2-3.8 and 5
extractions.evidence_summary: Direct one-for-one sale of FDUSD to the issuer requires an eligible FD121 account in good standing and compliance with the terms and applicable rules; the redemption right transfers with the token but is exercisable only after account eligibility and registration.
extractions.limitations: Retail and U.S. persons are excluded from direct services, and the reviewed terms do not supply a universal settlement time or public minimum.

extractions.locator: Sections 2.4 and 3.9; transparency section Built on a foundation of Trust
extractions.evidence_summary: Reserves are held through qualified custodians in segregated structures, but the terms state that FD121 beneficially owns the reserves and holders have no contractual or trust entitlement to reserve assets or their returns.
extractions.limitations: Operational segregation, custodian bankruptcy isolation, and holder ownership are distinct claims and must be scored separately.

extractions.locator: Sections 3.8, 7, and 14
extractions.evidence_summary: FD121 can restrict, defer, limit, suspend, or cancel issuance and redemption for reserve-liquidity stress, market disruption, legal or compliance concerns, fraud, or misconduct; blockchain forks or security problems may cause extended downtime.
extractions.limitations: The issuer retains broad discretion and provides no maximum duration for stress-related or blockchain-related suspension.

extractions.locator: Trade Strategies; backing and redemption-liquidity bullets
extractions.evidence_summary: USDe uses protocol backing assets with delta-neutral hedges rather than fiat reserves; Ethena reports that liquid stablecoins form a redemption buffer while the broader backing is held with multiple custodians and hedged through derivatives positions.
extractions.limitations: This design description does not provide a complete dated asset-by-asset weight table; numerical composition must use a contemporaneous dashboard snapshot.

extractions.locator: Custodian Attestations; current monthly reports
extractions.evidence_summary: Ethena publishes monthly custodian attestations addressing the existence, control, and value of USDe backing assets and reports that backing does not reside directly with derivatives exchanges.
extractions.limitations: Custodian attestations are not equivalent to a full financial-statement audit or fully onchain proof of every hedge and liability.

extractions.locator: Overview; whitelisting; pair availability; RFQ, fees, and error codes
extractions.evidence_summary: Direct minting and redemption use Ethena's API and smart contract, are limited to whitelisted wallets, support specified collateral pairs, incorporate quoted fees and gas, and remain subject to capacity, asset-availability, price-movement, and execution checks.
extractions.limitations: Non-whitelisted holders depend on secondary markets, and supported pairs, fees, capacity, and infrastructure can change.

extractions.locator: Custodian Attestations; backing-asset location statement
extractions.evidence_summary: Ethena states that backing assets are controlled through custodians and off-exchange settlement arrangements rather than deposited directly with derivatives exchanges; attestations test custody and control at monthly dates.
extractions.limitations: Custodial separation from exchanges does not itself prove bankruptcy remoteness, a direct holder claim, or segregation from every protocol-related creditor.

extractions.locator: Server location; RFQ and order-submission error codes
extractions.evidence_summary: Direct redemption depends on Ethena's hosted quoting infrastructure, wallet whitelisting, active collateral pairs, per-block capacity, timely signatures, sufficient balances and approvals, acceptable price movement, and successful onchain execution.
extractions.limitations: Operational controls are documented, but the source does not guarantee uptime or provide a recovery SLA during market, custodian, exchange, or cloud disruption.

extractions.locator: Protocol collateral and obligation dashboard; DAI/USDS system totals
extractions.evidence_summary: The live Sky financial dashboard exposes the protocol collateral and obligations supporting the combined DAI/USDS system, including collateral categories, position-level exposures, and excess coverage rather than a fixed fiat reserve basket.
extractions.limitations: DAI and USDS share protocol backing; asset-specific attribution must avoid double counting and preserve the dashboard snapshot date.

extractions.locator: Live protocol financial dashboard and underlying onchain positions
extractions.evidence_summary: DAI liabilities, vault collateral, liquidation parameters, and protocol positions are reconstructible from public smart-contract state and surfaced through the Sky financial dashboard.
extractions.limitations: Onchain observability verifies recorded state, not offchain asset value, legal enforceability, oracle accuracy, or absence of smart-contract defects.

extractions.locator: Peg Stability Module and collateral-vault mechanisms; Emergency Shutdown
extractions.evidence_summary: DAI has no universal issuer redemption account; liquidity comes through permissionless protocol modules, collateralized vault creation and repayment, and secondary markets, while emergency settlement provides a distinct collateral-claim process under shutdown conditions.
extractions.limitations: The foundational whitepaper predates later Sky migrations and modules; effective-date scoring must pair it with contemporaneous onchain configuration.

extractions.locator: Collateralized vaults, liquidation, and Emergency Shutdown sections
extractions.evidence_summary: Backing is locked or deployed under protocol rules rather than held in a corporate reserve account. Ordinary DAI does not represent title to a particular collateral asset; claims and allocation change under liquidation or emergency settlement mechanics.
extractions.limitations: Protocol control and onchain custody are not equivalent to legal segregation, and offchain real-world-asset structures introduce additional counterparties and legal claims.

extractions.locator: Liquidation, oracle security, governance, and Emergency Shutdown sections
extractions.evidence_summary: DAI conversion and collateral access depend on module liquidity, oracle operation, auctions, governance parameters, network execution, and smart-contract integrity; emergency shutdown can halt ordinary system operation and replace it with settlement procedures.
extractions.limitations: The source identifies mechanisms rather than uptime guarantees; current triggers and parameters must be read from effective onchain state.

extractions.locator: Protocol Collateral; data as of June 12, 2026
extractions.evidence_summary: Sky describes USDS as overcollateralized by a shared protocol portfolio spanning stablecoins, onchain and OTC crypto lending, short-duration Treasury exposure, high-grade corporate debt, and other approved structures, with live position detail on the financial dashboard.
extractions.limitations: Some exposures are indirect or offchain, and the published category mix changes with Agent deployment and governance decisions.

extractions.locator: Protocol collateral, obligations, and position-level financial dashboard
extractions.evidence_summary: The protocol publishes continuously inspectable onchain obligations, collateral positions, and risk parameters through its financial dashboard, enabling reconstruction without waiting for an issuer reserve attestation.
extractions.limitations: Onchain data does not independently verify offchain assets, legal wrappers, valuation models, or oracle inputs.

extractions.locator: Peg Stability Module; Common questions on conversion
extractions.evidence_summary: The permissionless Peg Stability Module supports one-for-one USDC/USDS conversion in both directions with governance-set fees currently reported as zero; the interface also describes single-transaction conversion without a USDS lock-up.
extractions.limitations: Execution depends on PSM liquidity, governance parameters, supported collateral, smart contracts, network gas, and frontend or direct-contract access.

extractions.locator: How USDS holds its peg; Protocol Collateral
extractions.evidence_summary: USDS is a protocol obligation backed by collateral controlled through smart contracts and governed structures, not a direct ownership claim on a segregated issuer bank account or on any particular collateral position.
extractions.limitations: Offchain Agent deployments can add custodial, contractual, and insolvency dependencies that onchain token balances alone do not resolve.

extractions.locator: USDC-USDS conversion; interface and governance disclaimers
extractions.evidence_summary: USDS conversion depends on live protocol contracts, PSM liquidity, governance-set parameters, supported routes, network availability, and gas. Sky.money is a non-custodial interface that does not control protocol contracts and may be unavailable even when direct contract access remains possible.
extractions.limitations: Protocol and interface availability are separate; governance can change fees, ceilings, collateral exposure, and other operating parameters.
